solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Cut ankle finally bound

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it follows, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: to lop is to cut off, as with branches
the last letter of ankle

explanation.surface: Someone has injured an ankle and had it strapped up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bound' reads as bandaged, partnering 'cut ankle', but it is the verb meaning to leap along.
explanation.definitionFit: To lope is to run with long, easy strides, which is a loose way of bounding along.

clue.text: Gentle soul’s first to cry over what may go on after dark?

definitions.text: what may go on after dark

indicators.note: first asks for the opening letter of the word before it and nothing more
in a down clue, over means turned over, so the letters run the opposite way

blocks.note: a light touch is a gentle one
the opening letter of soul
to blub is to sob, informally

explanation.surface: A tender-hearted person weeps over something that happens at night.
explanation.walkthrough: The soul's initial and the sob word are flipped together as one unit, not separately. 'Go on' is the punning definition: these are switched on after dark.
explanation.definitionFit: Electric bulbs are what people switch on once evening falls, so they literally go on at night.

clue.text: Murderer chewing over a charge, turning delusional

indicators.note: something chewing has another thing in its mouth, so one piece holds another
turning round makes the whole string face the other way, so read it backwards

blocks.note: Cain killed his brother Abel in Genesis
O is the cricket scorer's abbreviation for an over
taken as written
a rap is a criminal charge, as in a murder rap

explanation.surface: A killer brooding over the accusation against him starts losing his grip on reality.
explanation.walkthrough: CAIN takes O inside to make CAION, then A and RAP follow; the whole string CAIONARAP is then turned round. 'Over' is the cricket abbreviation, not a positional word.
explanation.definitionFit: A paranoiac suffers from paranoia, a mental state of irrational suspicion and false beliefs, so the word works as an adjective for delusional.

clue.text: Screen capturing India coach’s time-wasting tactic

indicators.note: to capture is to take something prisoner and hold it, so one piece goes inside another

blocks.note: to screen is to filter out
India is I in the NATO phonetic alphabet
a coach is a long-distance bus

explanation.surface: A TV screen catches the Indian cricket coach using a delaying ploy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'India coach' suggests a national sports manager, but the two words are separate pieces: a phonetic-alphabet letter and a vehicle.
explanation.definitionFit: A filibuster is a very long speech made in a legislature purely to delay or block a vote, a classic stalling ploy.

clue.text: Self-absorbed daughter not prepared to enter pub

indicators.note: entering means going inside, so these letters sit within the other piece

blocks.note: an inn is a pub
D is the standard abbreviation for daughter
raw food has not been prepared or cooked

explanation.surface: A moody daughter refuses to go into the pub with the family.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not prepared to' reads as unwilling, but 'not prepared' is RAW and 'to enter' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: Indrawn describes someone withdrawn into their own thoughts, an uncommon synonym for introspective or preoccupied with oneself.

clue.text: A deceit disguised something chilling

indicators.note: a disguise changes appearance, so these letters take on a new arrangement

blocks.note: the seven letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A trick concealed something sinister and frightening.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Chilling' suggests menace; here it means cooling, as a cold drink does.
explanation.definitionFit: Iced tea is a cold beverage, so it is literally something that cools you down on a hot day.

clue.text: Like a line of spilt Indian emulsion

indicators.note: spilt liquid ends up scattered in a mess, so these letters are jumbled

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: A streak of paint tipped over on the floor, perhaps an Indian-made emulsion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Line' sits naturally with spilt paint, but the definition is geometric: a line has only length.
explanation.definitionFit: A geometric line has length but no width or depth, so it has just one dimension.

clue.text: Skinny guy’s foremost obsession

indicators.note: foremost means at the very front, so only the opening letter is kept

blocks.note: skinny means thin
the opening letter of guy

explanation.surface: A thin man's chief fixation, perhaps food or exercise.
explanation.walkthrough: To have a thing about something is an idiom for being fixated on it.
explanation.definitionFit: Informally, having a thing about something means a fixation or preoccupation, so the noun can stand for an obsession.

clue.text: Step of ladder, right in the centre

indicators.note: the centre of a word is its middle, so only the middle letter is kept

blocks.note: a ladder in tights or stockings is a run
the middle letter of the five in right

explanation.surface: Directions for where to stand on a ladder: right in the middle.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Step of ladder' looks like the whole definition, but 'ladder' is wordplay: in British English a ladder is a run in tights. 'Right' gives its middle letter, not R.
explanation.definitionFit: A rung is one of the crossbars you tread on when climbing a ladder, so each one is a step.

clue.text: Look, Tom’s admitted to cheating, OK?

indicators.note: being admitted means let inside, so these letters go within the other word

blocks.note: fiddling is cheating, as in fiddling the books
an air is a look or manner
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone reproaches Tom, who has confessed to cheating: is that acceptable?
explanation.walkthrough: 'Admitted to' reads as confessed, but it is the container signal, and the inserted pair goes in after the cheating word's first letter.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair to middling is an idiom meaning moderately good or passable, which is what calling something just about acceptable conveys.

clue.text: Delta stops fish reaching a lake

blocks.note: the gar is a long-snouted fish
Delta is D in the NATO phonetic alphabet
taken as written

explanation.surface: A river delta prevents fish from getting through to a lake.
explanation.walkthrough: D 'stops' GAR in the sense of closing it off at the end, and A follows. 'Delta' and 'lake' feel like one watery scene, but the lake is the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Garda is the largest lake in Italy, a popular holiday spot, so it is a specific example of a lake.

clue.text: The German artist’s consumer’s guide

blocks.note: die is a German word for the
Titian was the great Venetian painter

explanation.surface: A buyer's handbook to the paintings of a German artist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Consumer's guide' suggests a shopping handbook; the consumer here is someone eating food.
explanation.definitionFit: A dietitian is a nutrition expert who advises people on what to eat, guiding those who consume food.

clue.text: What you may need to print or redo, retracting blunders

definitions.text: What you may need to print

indicators.note: to blunder is to stumble about clumsily, so these letters fall into a different order

blocks.note: the fourteen letters to rearrange

explanation.surface: Advice for a writer: publish, or rework the piece while withdrawing its errors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Blunders' looks like a noun being retracted; it is a verb acting on the two words before it.
explanation.definitionFit: A laser printer cannot produce pages without a supply of powdered ink held in a replaceable unit.

clue.text: Attempted to gobble pie up outside United’s ground

indicators.note: gobbling swallows food whole, so one piece takes another inside
being outside means surrounding, so these letters wrap round another
in a down clue, up means read from the bottom, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: attempted means tried
a tart is a pie
the first letter of United, used as its short form in football club names

explanation.surface: A fan at a football ground tries to wolf down a pie outside the stadium.
explanation.walkthrough: The pie wraps United first and only then is that unit turned upwards before going inside. 'Ground' feels like a football stadium but is the past tense of grind.
explanation.definitionFit: Triturated means reduced to fine powder by rubbing or crushing, a technical synonym for milled or pulverised.

clue.text: One imagined being unoriginal, taking year off after college

indicators.note: taking something off removes it, so the abbreviation for year disappears

blocks.note: uni is short for university
corny means trite and unoriginal

explanation.surface: A student fancied themselves as derivative, taking a gap year after university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Taking year off after college' evokes a gap year; Y for year is removed from CORNY. 'One imagined being' should be read as a single noun phrase: an imaginary creature.
explanation.definitionFit: The unicorn is a mythical horse with a single horn, a creature that exists only in legend and fancy.

clue.text: Supporter in a cap

blocks.note: taken as written
to cap a story is to better it, outdoing it

explanation.surface: A fan in the crowd wearing a baseball cap.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cap' looks like headgear but is a verb, to top or outdo someone.
explanation.definitionFit: An abetter is one who encourages or assists another, especially in wrongdoing, so they back or help that person.

clue.text: Class-A drug taken up to escape

indicators.note: in a down clue, taken up means lifted from the bottom, so the letters read backwards

blocks.note: pot is slang for cannabis
flight is running away

explanation.surface: Someone takes a hard drug in order to escape reality.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Class-A drug' reads as one legal category of narcotic, but the hyphenated pair is the definition and 'drug' starts the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: Top-flight means of the highest rank or quality, just as first-class or class-A does.

clue.text: Gambling on promotion

blocks.note: first meaning: placing a bet on a horse or team
second meaning: support or endorsement given to a cause

explanation.walkthrough: The surface suggests betting on getting a promotion at work; the two halves are separate meanings, a verb phrase and a noun.
explanation.definitionFit: To back a horse is to bet on it, and backing as a noun is the support or championing given to something.

clue.text: Troop member that’s into acting, or ill-advised

indicators.note: something that is into a phrase sits inside it, so the letters are found within the words

blocks.note: spans the end of the first word, the whole of the next two and the start of the last

explanation.surface: A soldier who has taken up amateur dramatics, perhaps unwisely.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Troop' is not a military unit here but a group of apes. 'Into' doubles as 'keen on' in the surface.
explanation.definitionFit: Gorillas live in family groups called troops, so any individual great ape in one belongs to that group.

clue.text: Fine clock broken by American old woman

indicators.note: a thing broken by another is split open with the intruder lodged inside

blocks.note: F is the abbreviation for fine, as on pencils
US stands for American
to clock is slang for to notice or spot

explanation.surface: An elderly American lady breaks a valuable timepiece.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Clock' is a verb, to spot. 'Old woman' is a disparaging label for a fussy person of either sex.
explanation.definitionFit: Calling someone an old woman means they are timid and overly particular, which is exactly what a fusspot is.

clue.text: Penalty leads to striker showing extra skill

indicators.note: leads are the front runners, so the opening letters of the words that follow are taken

blocks.note: a fine is a monetary penalty
the opening letters of those three words

explanation.surface: A penalty kick lets a footballer show off his flair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Penalty' feels like a football spot kick but is a monetary fine. 'Leads to' looks like 'results in' but signals first letters.
explanation.definitionFit: Finesse is refined delicacy and dexterity in handling something, a close synonym for skill or deftness.

clue.text: Chap almost venturing to nick neckwear

indicators.note: almost means not quite all, so the last letter is dropped

blocks.note: a chap is a man
daring means bold, venturing
to nick and to collar both mean to arrest

explanation.surface: A man very nearly sets out to steal a tie or scarf.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Nick' suggests stealing, but it is British slang for arrest, as is 'collar'.
explanation.definitionFit: A mandarin collar is a short, stand-up band round the neck of a shirt or jacket, Chinese in style.

clue.text: Burning desire of a man to drop gym classes

indicators.note: to drop something is to let it go, so these letters are removed

blocks.note: taken as written
a man is a person
PE is physical education, the school gym lesson

explanation.surface: A man longs to give up his sessions at the gym.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Burning desire' reads as one phrase, but only 'Burning' defines; 'desire of' links it to the wordplay, where PE leaves A PERSON.
explanation.definitionFit: Arson is the crime of deliberately setting fire to property, a specific kind of criminal burning.

clue.text: Starter of stuffed sweet potato

indicators.note: a starter comes first, so only the opening letter is taken

blocks.note: the opening letter of stuffed
pud is short for pudding, a dessert

explanation.surface: A menu offering stuffed sweet potato as the first course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Sweet potato' looks like one vegetable; 'sweet' is a noun meaning dessert, which British speakers call pud.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is an informal everyday name for a potato in Britain and elsewhere.

clue.text: Gums filled with bad things to suck

indicators.note: something filled with stuff has it inside, so one piece holds another

blocks.note: pastes and gums are both adhesives
ill means bad, as in ill effects

explanation.surface: Diseased gums packed with nasty matter that needs drawing out.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Gums' suggests the mouth, which suits sucking, but here it means glues.
explanation.definitionFit: Pastilles are small sweets or medicated lozenges meant to dissolve slowly in the mouth.

clue.text: Ancient craft spoken of in esoteric terms

indicators.note: something spoken is heard rather than read, so the sound matters, not the spelling

blocks.note: the Argo was the ship of Jason and the Argonauts

explanation.surface: An old trade or skill described using obscure jargon.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Craft' suggests a skill or trade, but it is a vessel. The final T of the answer is silent, as in French.
explanation.definitionFit: Argot is the private slang or jargon of a particular group, vocabulary that outsiders cannot follow.

clue.text: One irritated by study and run down

blocks.note: a den is a study, a private room for work
I is the Roman numeral one
to grate is to irritate

explanation.surface: Someone annoyed by too much studying feels exhausted.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Run down' reads as worn out, but means belittled. 'By' places the study piece beside the rest, ahead of it.
explanation.definitionFit: To run someone down is to criticise or disparage them, which is exactly what denigrating does.

clue.text: Credit notes dismissed by academic’s boss

indicators.note: dismissed means sent away, so these letters leave the word that follows

blocks.note: studious means academic, given to study
IOUs are written promises to pay, notes recording credit

explanation.surface: A university chief cancels the credit notes issued by a lecturer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Boss' suggests a manager, but here it is a knob or stud on a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: A boss is a raised ornamental knob, as on a shield or ceiling, and a stud is the same kind of projecting knob.
